definition: LeNet is a series of convolutional neural network architectures created by a research group at AT&T Bell Laboratories between of the period of 1988 to 1998, centered around Yann LeCun.
details: They were designed for reading small grayscale images of handwritten digits and letters, and were used in ATMs for reading cheques. Convolutional neural networks are a kind of feed-forward neural network whose artificial neurons can respond to a part of the surrounding cells in the coverage range and perform well in large-scale image processing. LeNet-5 was one of the earliest convolutional neural networks and was historically important during the development of deep learning. In general, when LeNet is referred to without a number, it refers to the 1998 version, LeNet-5, which is the most well-known version.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — LeNet — is what makes everything else possible.
